evidence.title: Intended use
evidence.statement: RhythmReview analyses a 30-second single-lead ECG recording to assist a qualified clinician in identifying possible atrial fibrillation in adults aged 22 and over. It is not intended for continuous monitoring, emergency use, or standalone diagnosis.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled intended use evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Possible AF indication
evidence.statement: RhythmReview identifies ECG recordings that may show atrial fibrillation for clinician review.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled claim evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Three controlled outcomes
evidence.statement: The application reports Possible AF, No AF detected, or Unreadable recording.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled claim evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Time to result
evidence.statement: For supported recordings, the application returns a result within 30 seconds after upload completes.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled claim evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Clinician decision support
evidence.statement: The result informs but does not replace clinical judgement or diagnostic confirmation.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled claim evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Upload a short ECG
evidence.statement: The clinician needs to submit a 30-second single-lead ECG without reformatting the signal.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Recognise unusable signals
evidence.statement: The clinician needs a clear indication when signal quality is insufficient for analysis.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Interpret the result correctly
evidence.statement: The clinician needs result wording that makes the need for professional review unambiguous.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Receive a timely result
evidence.statement: The clinician needs a result quickly enough to use during the active review workflow.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Know the use limitations
evidence.statement: The clinician needs visible warnings that RhythmReview is not for emergencies or standalone diagnosis.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Trust the analysed version
evidence.statement: The clinician needs the application to use only the released and validated algorithm version.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Protect ECG data
evidence.statement: The organisation needs ECG recordings and results protected during transfer and storage.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Review an accountable history
evidence.statement: Quality staff need an audit history of uploads, results, acknowledgements, and released versions.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled user need evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Supported recording duration
evidence.statement: The system shall accept a single-lead ECG recording with a duration of 30 seconds ± 1 second.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Supported sampling rate
evidence.statement: The system shall accept sampling rates from 250 Hz through 500 Hz and reject unsupported rates.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Signal quality gate
evidence.statement: The system shall classify a recording as Unreadable when the released signal-quality threshold is not met.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Maximum analysis time
evidence.statement: The system shall display a controlled result no later than 30 seconds after a valid upload completes.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Controlled timeout
evidence.statement: The system shall stop analysis and display a controlled failure message if no result is available after 35 seconds.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Permitted result classes
evidence.statement: The system shall produce only Possible AF, No AF detected, or Unreadable recording.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Possible AF display copy
evidence.statement: For a positive triage result, the interface shall display “Possible AF” and a clinician-review prompt.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Result acknowledgement
evidence.statement: The system shall require the clinician to acknowledge the result before closing the review.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Emergency-use warning
evidence.statement: The upload screen shall state that RhythmReview is not intended for emergency assessment.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Audit event capture
evidence.statement: The system shall record the user, timestamp, model version, input identifier, result, and acknowledgement event.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Transport encryption
evidence.statement: The system shall protect ECG and result data in transit using the organisation’s approved encrypted protocol.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Role restriction
evidence.statement: Only users assigned the clinician role shall initiate ECG analysis or view patient-linked results.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Locked model version
evidence.statement: Production analysis shall execute only the algorithm version identified in the approved release baseline.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Internal confidence handling
evidence.statement: Internal confidence values shall not be presented as diagnostic probabilities to the clinician.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Recording retention
evidence.statement: The service shall delete uploaded ECG payloads after the configured clinical retention period expires.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Recoverable service failure
evidence.statement: The interface shall preserve the upload reference and permit a controlled retry after a transient service failure.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled requirement evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: False negative delays care
evidence.statement: A false No AF detected result may delay further clinical assessment.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: False positive drives unnecessary action
evidence.statement: A false Possible AF result may lead to unnecessary testing or treatment.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Late result disrupts review
evidence.statement: An unexpectedly delayed result may cause the clinician to proceed without reviewing the output.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Poor signal produces misleading result
evidence.statement: An artefact-heavy recording may be classified instead of rejected as unreadable.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Unsupported population used
evidence.statement: Performance may be unknown when the application is used outside the validated adult population.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Decision-support result treated as diagnosis
evidence.statement: A user may treat the triage output as diagnostic confirmation.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: ECG data disclosed
evidence.statement: ECG recordings or result data may be exposed to an unauthorised party.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Service unavailable during review
evidence.statement: Loss of service may interrupt a clinician’s review workflow.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled hazard evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Sensitivity acceptance criterion
evidence.statement: Release testing shall demonstrate sensitivity at or above the approved threshold for the intended population.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Specificity acceptance criterion
evidence.statement: Release testing shall demonstrate specificity at or above the approved threshold for the intended population.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Visible analysis timer
evidence.statement: The interface shall show analysis progress and a controlled timeout message before the workflow deadline.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Signal quality rejection
evidence.statement: The quality gate shall route low-quality recordings to Unreadable before rhythm classification.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Population restriction
evidence.statement: Labelling and interface controls shall restrict use to adults aged 22 and over.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Decision-support disclaimer
evidence.statement: Every result view shall state that the output requires clinician interpretation and is not a diagnosis.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Encryption and access control
evidence.statement: The service shall combine encrypted transport, least-privilege roles, and access logging.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Controlled retry path
evidence.statement: Service failures shall produce a safe state with no clinical classification and an explicit retry option.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Released-model enforcement
evidence.statement: Deployment shall block models whose identifier is absent from the approved release configuration.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled risk control evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Upload gateway
evidence.statement: Validates file shape, duration, sampling metadata, role, and transfer integrity before accepting an ECG.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled component evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Analysis orchestrator
evidence.statement: Coordinates quality assessment, locked-model inference, timing control, and result persistence.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled component evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Clinician result panel
evidence.statement: Renders the three permitted results, review prompt, limitations, and acknowledgement control.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled component evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Timeout supervisor
evidence.statement: Tracks elapsed analysis time and transitions the request to a controlled failure state.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled component evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Audit ledger
evidence.statement: Stores immutable workflow events and released component identifiers.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled component evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: PDF evidence exporter
evidence.statement: Produces an administrative PDF copy of completed audit events for internal review.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled component evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Telemetry monitor
evidence.statement: Collects service health and analysis-latency metrics without ECG signal payloads.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled component evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Recording boundary verification
evidence.statement: Verify acceptance at 29, 30, and 31 seconds and rejection outside the specified tolerance.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Sampling-rate verification
evidence.statement: Verify supported and unsupported sampling rates at every boundary.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Analysis-time verification
evidence.statement: Verify the 95th percentile and worst-case valid-upload result time remain at or below 30 seconds.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Timeout verification
evidence.statement: Verify analysis stops at 35 seconds and produces no rhythm classification.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Result-copy verification
evidence.statement: Verify each controlled output and clinician-review prompt against the approved copy specification.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Signal-quality challenge
evidence.statement: Verify noisy, truncated, flat-line, and saturated signals are routed to Unreadable.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Clinical workflow validation
evidence.statement: Representative clinicians shall correctly interpret each output and its limitations in simulated use.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Failure recovery verification
evidence.statement: Verify retry behaviour after network, inference, and persistence failures.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Legacy timing result
evidence.statement: Historical build RR-0.8 returned results within 45 seconds under the retired infrastructure.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Security control verification
evidence.statement: Verify transport encryption, access restrictions, and audit records in the release environment.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Model-version enforcement
evidence.statement: Verify unapproved model identifiers cannot enter service and produce no result.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Retention verification
evidence.statement: Verify ECG payload deletion at the configured retention boundary while audit metadata remains.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled test evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Adult performance study
evidence.statement: Retrospective multi-site study supporting AF triage performance in adults aged 22 and over.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled clinical evidence evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Subgroup analysis
evidence.statement: Performance analysis by age, sex, site, device source, and clinically relevant rhythm subgroup.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled clinical evidence evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Clinical workflow study
evidence.statement: Simulated-use study assessing result interpretation, acknowledgement, and referral decisions by clinicians.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled clinical evidence evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Possible AF result label
evidence.statement: Possible AF. Review the ECG and assess the patient using your clinical judgement.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled label evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Time-to-result statement
evidence.statement: RhythmReview usually provides a result within 35 seconds of upload.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled label evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Clinical claim statement
evidence.statement: RhythmReview confirms atrial fibrillation from a single-lead ECG recording.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled label evidence for RhythmReview.

evidence.title: Use limitation
evidence.statement: For adults aged 22 and over. Not for emergencies, continuous monitoring, or use as a standalone diagnosis.
evidence.rationale: Defines controlled label evidence for RhythmReview.

scenarios.title: Clarify result wording
scenarios.proposedText: Possible atrial fibrillation; clinician review required.
scenarios.rationale: Make the result explicit and reduce the chance that a user reads the abbreviation as a diagnosis.

drafts.text: Possible atrial fibrillation; clinician review required.
For a positive triage result, the interface shall display “Possible atrial fibrillation; clinician review required.”
Renders the three permitted results, including the controlled Possible atrial fibrillation wording and clinician-review requirement, plus limitations and the acknowledgement control.
Verify the exact text of each controlled output and clinician-review prompt, including “Possible atrial fibrillation; clinician review required.”, against the approved copy specification.

scenarios.presenter: Start with a wording change that looks trivial. Follow the path from label to interface requirement, result panel, and copy verification. Point out that the algorithm and clinical performance evidence stay out of the update set.

scenarios.title: Extend analysis time
scenarios.proposedText: The system shall display a controlled result no later than 60 seconds after a valid upload completes.
scenarios.rationale: Support a more computationally demanding released algorithm while preserving a controlled clinician workflow.

drafts.text: The system shall display a controlled result no later than 60 seconds after a valid upload completes.
Coordinates quality assessment, locked-model inference, result persistence, and timing control for a maximum 60-second result window.
Verify that the 95th percentile and worst-case valid-upload result time remain at or below 60 seconds.
Verify that analysis stops at 65 seconds and produces no rhythm classification when no controlled result is available.
RhythmReview provides a controlled result within 60 seconds of a valid upload.
The system shall stop analysis and display a controlled failure message if no result is available after 65 seconds.
Tracks elapsed analysis time, enforces the 60-second result deadline, and transitions the request to a controlled failure state at 65 seconds.
Representative clinicians shall correctly interpret each output and its limitations in simulated use with result delivery times up to 60 seconds.

scenarios.presenter: Change one performance requirement from 30 to 60 seconds. Show deterministic trace paths first, then the related items found from text. Review the timeout contradiction and the effect on clinical workflow validation.

scenarios.title: Expand to adolescents
scenarios.proposedText: RhythmReview analyses a 30-second single-lead ECG recording to assist a qualified clinician in identifying possible atrial fibrillation in patients aged 12 and over.
scenarios.rationale: Expand the intended population to include adolescent patients aged 12 through 21.

drafts.text: RhythmReview analyses a 30-second single-lead ECG recording to assist a qualified clinician in identifying possible atrial fibrillation in patients aged 12 and over. It is not intended for continuous monitoring, emergency use, or standalone diagnosis.
The system shall accept a single-lead ECG recording with a duration of 30 seconds ± 1 second for each age group in the approved population.
The system shall classify a recording as Unreadable when the released signal-quality threshold validated for the approved population is not met.
The upload screen shall state that RhythmReview is not intended for emergency assessment and is approved only for patients aged 12 and over.
Verify that noisy, truncated, flat-line, and saturated signals from adult and adolescent validation sets are routed to Unreadable.
Representative clinicians shall correctly interpret each output, its limitations, and the use of RhythmReview for patients aged 12 and over in simulated use.

scenarios.presenter: Use the population expansion to test recall. The change must reach clinical evidence, subgroup performance, risk, usability, labelling, and validation. A polished wording update alone is a failure.

suggestions.rationale: The controlled result label is the wording being changed and needs a new approved version.
The display requirement contains the old “Possible AF” copy and must match the proposed wording.
The result panel renders the controlled copy and clinician-review prompt, so its design description must match the revised text.
Copy verification must be rerun against the newly approved result wording and clinician-review prompt.
QA must confirm that the new text still makes professional review unambiguous.
QA must confirm that spelling out atrial fibrillation does not change the approved three-outcome claim.
The maximum result time is the controlled requirement being changed from 30 to 60 seconds.
QA must confirm that a 60-second result still supports the active clinician review workflow.
The longer result window may increase the chance that a clinician proceeds before reviewing the output.
The progress indicator and timeout message must remain effective across the longer analysis window.
The orchestrator enforces analysis timing and must support the new 60-second result deadline.
Timing verification uses the old 30-second acceptance limit and must be rerun at 60 seconds.
The current 35-second timeout conflicts with a permitted 60-second analysis and needs a new boundary test.
The time-to-result label says 35 seconds and must agree with the new controlled timing claim.
The 35-second controlled timeout would stop analysis before the proposed 60-second result deadline.
The timeout supervisor implements the current 35-second limit and must enforce the revised boundaries.
Workflow validation must confirm that clinicians can use results delivered near the new 60-second limit.
The intended population is being expanded from adults aged 22 and over to patients aged 12 and over.
QA must confirm that the indication is supported for adolescents before the population claim changes.
QA must confirm that the decision-support limitation remains adequate for adolescent use.
QA must confirm that adolescent recordings use the same supported format and duration.
QA must review whether clinicians need different result interpretation guidance for adolescent patients.
The user need for visible limitations must cover the expanded age boundary.
The recording input requirement must be reviewed for the expanded population and its validation data.
Signal-quality thresholds may perform differently in adolescent ECG recordings and need controlled evidence.
The upload warning must state the revised lower age boundary with the existing emergency-use limitation.
False-negative risk must be reassessed for adolescents because adult performance cannot be assumed.
False-positive risk must be reassessed for adolescents because prevalence and performance may differ.
The unsupported-population hazard changes directly when patients aged 12 through 21 enter the intended use.
The sensitivity acceptance criterion must be reviewed against evidence for the expanded population.
The specificity acceptance criterion must be reviewed against evidence for the expanded population.
The population restriction control must change from adults aged 22 and over and gain verification coverage.
Signal-quality challenge testing must include representative adolescent recordings.
Clinical workflow validation must cover clinicians interpreting results for adolescent patients.
The adult performance study does not support patients aged 12 through 21 and needs a documented applicability review.
The subgroup analysis must add and evaluate the adolescent age groups in the proposed population.
